content: coffee A controlled blast on a movie set near London’s O2 arena ignited a fire that wrecked a van and badly damaged a car and a lorry. Fire crews were summoned to an open‑air yard on Dock Road in Silvertown just before 8 p.m. on Saturday, and after about an hour the flames were brought under control with the help of around twenty‑five firefighters; no one was hurt. Officials said the blaze stemmed from a pre‑arranged filming activity taking place close to the venue that will host upcoming shows by Niall Horan and Texas. The London Fire Brigade posted on X that the fire in the Silvertown yard is now contained, noting that one vehicle was destroyed while most of a car and a lorry suffered damage, and that there are no injury reports. They added that the fire originated from a controlled explosion on the set that escaped control, that firefighters acted swiftly to put it out, and that crews will stay on site for the rest of the evening. The yard lies near the Thames cable‑car link, and a Metropolitan Police spokesman said they are aware of reports of explosions heard close to the O2 in Greenwich.
